scenarios.text: A colonist with a hauling job has a route that crosses a fallen wire lying on the ground. The wire's end still connects through the remaining conduit to a running generator and is sparking. The colonist walks over the sparking end and takes an electric shock.
scenarios.expect: accept: a live fallen wire shocks anyone crossing it on another job

scenarios.text: A colonist is assigned the re-string job on a live fallen wire (end still connected to a running generator and sparking). The colonist walks up to the sparking end intending to fix it and is shocked on arrival, falling down.
scenarios.expect: reject: the fixer is safe; shocking the re-stringer is red

scenarios.text: A fallen wire lies on the ground. Its end is cut off from every power source (no generator, battery or solar anywhere on that side, none connected). A visiting trader walks over the end and is shocked.
scenarios.expect: reject: a dead fallen wire shocks no one

scenarios.text: A powered conduit line is fed by a generator on the west side only. No battery, generator or other source exists on the east side. A conduit cell in the middle is destroyed by a mortar. Afterwards the west end sparks and the east end sparks too.
scenarios.expect: reject: the east end has no path to any power source so it must lie dead

scenarios.text: A conduit line has a generator on the west side and a battery (charged, connected) on the east side. A conduit cell in the middle is destroyed. Afterwards both loose ends spark and no cord crosses the gap.
scenarios.expect: accept: each side has its own source so both ends spark

scenarios.text: After a conduit cell is destroyed, a cord is still drawn straight across the gap between the two ends, as though the line were unbroken. Power on both sides still works as normal.
scenarios.expect: reject: no cord across the gap after a cut

scenarios.text: A player walks from one game into a new game in the same session. In the first game they had clamped a power tap on a neighbour's line and a pawn of that neighbour saw it. In the second game, on a colony with no tap built, goodwill with a faction starts draining steadily because the old tap is still registered.
scenarios.expect: reject: nothing of one game carries into the next

scenarios.text: A player picks the Industrial look for a run in game one, quits to menu, and starts a new game in the same session. They build a new run in the new game without choosing anything. The new run is drawn in Industrial because it reuses the earlier game's pick.
scenarios.expect: reject: runs take fresh looks, not the old game's style picks

scenarios.text: A player sees a base with a plain conduit run and a waterproof conduit run in Modern look at play zoom. No vanilla pipe graphic is visible on either run, only loose cords, and the power overlay still draws its connector lines when toggled on.
scenarios.expect: accept: conduit draws no pipe; overlay still works

scenarios.text: At play zoom in Industrial look, a waterproof conduit run is drawn with the vanilla pipe graphic visible beneath the cords. Plain conduit runs show no pipe.
scenarios.expect: reject: waterproof conduit must be invisible too

scenarios.text: In Modern look, a 3-way conduit junction in a workshop is drawn as the vanilla splitter box with cords passing by it. No power strip is drawn there.
scenarios.expect: reject: Modern junctions get the long power strip, not the splitter box

scenarios.text: A 3-way junction in the Modern look shows a long power strip with two cords plugged in plus the strip's own lead going on to the rest of the net. A tester thinks only two cords are plugged in so something is missing.
scenarios.expect: accept: at a 3-way the strip takes two cords plus its own lead

scenarios.text: A pump sits directly beside a conduit cell and is powered by that adjacent conduit. At play zoom a cord runs from the pump to the net, and a second, separate cable also hangs off the pump going to nowhere connected.
scenarios.expect: reject: no phantom second cable at an adjacent-fed pump

scenarios.text: A cord reaches a water pump that has a pipe port on its south face. The cord approaches diagonally from the north-east and slides underneath the pump, entering nowhere near the port. The cord's route from the generator is a long winding detour three times the straight distance.
scenarios.expect: accept: diagonal approach sliding under is wanted; circuitous route is allowed

scenarios.text: On a 2000-conduit-cell base, a colonist digs past a wire and the cord rebuild takes about 140 ms on the main thread on the owner's machine, producing a visible hitch each time.
scenarios.expect: reject: lone rebuild must cost at most 20 ms a frame

scenarios.text: A player clamps a power tap onto a neighbouring faction's line and builds it. A pawn of that neighbour sees the clamp. Goodwill with that same neighbour drops once by 10 and then stays flat for the following days while the clamp remains.
scenarios.expect: reject: caught tap should drain goodwill steadily, not one-off

scenarios.text: A colonist cuts a conduit run in the middle. The near side is still joined to the base generator. The far side has no generator but does have its own charged battery wired to it. After the cut, no cord is drawn across the gap. The near-side end sparks. The far-side end hangs limp and unsparking, because the builder reasoned that the generator is the only real source. Is this drawing right?
scenarios.expect: reject: the far end still reaches a power source (its own battery), so it must spark too; a powered end drawn limp is wrong

scenarios.text: A conduit run is cut. The far side has no generator, battery or any other power source. Its cut end sparks anyway, matching the near end, so the cut reads as symmetrical. No cord is drawn across the gap. Is this drawing right?
scenarios.expect: reject: an end cut off from all power that sparks is wrong

scenarios.text: A fallen span lies on the ground with a live sparking end. A colonist is on a haul job whose route passes over that end. A second colonist is on a job to repair a different cut span elsewhere, and his path also crosses the same sparking end. Neither is walking to re-string this wire. Neither is shocked. The design is judged on this behaviour. Does it pass?
scenarios.expect: reject: only a pawn approaching intending to fix the sparking line is safe; anyone incidentally crossing it on a different job is shocked, including the repair colonist working on another wire

scenarios.text: Chemfuel is spilled on the cell under a fallen wire's end. That end is dead, because its side has no power source. It does not spark and the fuel does not ignite. Next to it, an identical spill sits under a live sparking end of another fallen wire, and that fuel catches fire. Is this behaviour correct?
scenarios.expect: accept: fuel ignites under a live sparking end and not under a dead wire

scenarios.text: A tap is clamped onto a neighbouring faction's line. The faction's pawns see it. Their goodwill with the player drops once by 10 points at the moment of discovery, then stays flat for the following days while the tap keeps drawing their power. Power does flow from their line to the tap. Does this satisfy the design?
scenarios.expect: reject: the owner asked for a steady goodwill drain while the tap is seen (like living too close to a settlement), not a one-off drop

scenarios.text: In one session the player picks the Industrial look and clamps a tap in game one. They then return to the menu and start a brand-new game in the same session without restarting RimWorld. The new game opens with Industrial still selected and the old tap's record still held, though it has no visible effect yet. Is the new game's start state acceptable?
scenarios.expect: reject: nothing from one game, no tap and no style pick, may carry into the next game started in the same session

scenarios.text: A Modern-look base has a 4-way conduit junction. A long power strip is drawn beside it. Three cords are plugged into the strip, and the fourth cord ends on the junction cell centre next to the strip, unplugged. A plain 2-way corner elsewhere has no strip drawn. Is the 4-way junction right?
scenarios.expect: reject: every cord at a 3- or 4-way junction must be plugged into the joining piece; the unplugged fourth cord fails (the corner with no strip is fine)

scenarios.text: On a 2000-cell base, a burst of 50 simultaneous wire placements averages 8 ms a frame. A single lone wire placement or cut costs 35 ms a frame. The reported figure is the average over a long window, which is 9 ms a frame. Does the rewire cost pass?
scenarios.expect: reject: the lone rebuild must cost at most 20 ms a frame; the average and burst hide the stall

scenarios.text: A pump has a conduit on the cell directly adjacent to it, and is fed by that conduit. Two cords are drawn near it. One runs to the pump. A second, longer cord also runs to the pump but is drawn as if it were a separate disconnected line from the net. The builder says the owner allowed circuitous cord routes. Is this right?
scenarios.expect: reject: no phantom second cable at an adjacent-fed pump; the owner's allowance covers only route, not an extra cable acting disconnected

scenarios.text: Cords run along a room wall. They pile against the wall, but every cord stops one full cell short of the wall. Nothing is drawn across the wall or rock. A device on the far side of the wall is joined to the net, and the player sees no cord crossing the wall. Is the wall treatment right?
scenarios.expect: reject: cords must end at the wall face; stopping a cell short does not meet the face
